title: Nanopore nCoV-2019 Sequencing Protocol with RAPID Barcoding
author: Anton Pembaur
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.b3bcqiiw
materials: For whole genome sequencing using combined RT-PCR, samples with a Ct <20 are suitable. Higher Ct values ≤26 can be suitable as well, but we strongly recommend verification of the amplicon quality utilizing gelelectrophresis and/or microcapillary electrophoresis (Agilent) after combined RT-PCR. Isolate RNA using any suitable protocol. We tried magnetic Bead based (Nimbus/TanBead), spin collum based (QIAamp Viral RNA, Qiagen) and trizol/chloroforme extraction, with no significant differences.
Pool all barcoded samples, noting the total volume.

For whole genome sequencing using combined RT-PCR, samples with a Ct <20 are suitable. Higher Ct values ≤26 can be suitable as well, but we strongly recommend verification of the amplicon quality utilizing gelelectrophresis and/or microcapillary electrophoresis (Agilent) after combined RT-PCR. Isolate RNA using any suitable protocol. We tried magnetic Bead based (Nimbus/TanBead), spin collum based (QIAamp Viral RNA, Qiagen) and trizol/chloroforme extraction, with no significant differences.

steps.title: Prepare RT-PCR Reaction
steps.instruction: Prepare the RT-PCR reaction in a new PCR tube using the following components for the Luna Universal Probe One-Step RT-qPCR Kit (2X) (or Luna Probe One-Step RT-qPCR 4X Mix with UDG, adjusting volumes accordingly):

substeps.instruction: Add 10 µL Luna Universal Probe One-Step Reaction Mix (2X)
Add 1 µL Luna Enzyme Mix (20X)
Add 1 µL Primer Pool1 or Pool2
Add up to 8 µL Sample (depending on Ct Value and concentration)
Fill up to 20 µL with Nuclease free H2O

steps.title: Perform Thermal Cycling
steps.instruction: Set up and run the following program on the thermal cycler:

substeps.instruction: Reverse Transcription: 55 °C for 00:30:00 (1 cycle)
Heat Activation: 95 °C for 00:01:00 (1 cycle)
Denaturation: 95 °C for 00:00:20 (34 cycles for Pool 1, 30 cycles for Pool 2)
Annealing and Extension: 60 °C for 00:03:30 (34 cycles for Pool 1, 30 cycles for Pool 2)
Final Extension: 65 °C for 00:05:00 (1 cycle)
Hold: 4 °C Indefinite

steps.title: Quantify PCR Products
steps.instruction: Quantify each PCR reaction using a Qubit fluorometer (Nanodrop is not recommended).

steps.title: Pool PCR Reactions
steps.instruction: Pool the two PCR reactions for each sample in a new PCR tube.

substeps.instruction: Combine 200 ng from each sample to a total amount of 400 ng
Add nuclease free water to reach a total volume of 7.5 µL

steps.title: Perform Rapid Barcoding
steps.instruction: Set up the following reaction for each sample (up to 12 samples) using the SQK-RBK004 Rapid Barcoding Kit:

substeps.instruction: Combine 7.5 µL DNA amplicons (100 ng total) with 2.5 µL Fragmentation Mix RB01-12 (specific to each sample) for a total volume of 10 µL
Mix gently by flicking the tube and spin down
Incubate in a PCR machine: 30 °C for 00:01:00, then 80 °C for 00:01:00, then 4 °C for 00:00:30

steps.title: Clean Up Amplicons
steps.instruction: Perform an Ampure XP Bead Cleanup using a 1:1 ratio of sample to beads.

steps.title: Attach Adapter
steps.instruction: Add 1 µL of RAP (from the RBK004 kit) to 10 µL of the cleaned, barcoded DNA from the previous step.

substeps.instruction: Mix gently by flicking the tube and spin down
Incubate the reaction for 00:05:00 at room temperature

steps.title: Load and Sequence Library
steps.instruction: Load the prepared library into a MinION flow cell (FLO-MIN106D) according to the Oxford Nanopore Rapid Barcoding (RBK004) protocol.

substeps.instruction: Store the library on ice until ready to load
Start the sequencing run using MinKNOW
Enable real-time basecalling and demultiplexing in MinKNOW or use RAMPART on a LINUX environment
Sequence until approximately 10,000 to 20,000 reads (10-20 Mb) per sample are achieved
